value.topic: Rationale for the reorganization creating Morningstar Wealth Management, led by Daniel Needham, and how it involves Managed Portfolios, Retail (Morningstar.com), Direct Indexing, and ByAllAccounts
value.stated_position: Management said changing investor demographics and preferences, advancing technological capabilities, and increasing investment options are significantly impacting the advisor client segment, and that the intent to bring these capabilities together "is all about removing friction and making it easier for advisors to respond to evolving end investor expectations." The launch of Morningstar Wealth Management combines Morningstar Managed Portfolios, Morningstar Office, ByAllAccounts, and Morningstar.com; management noted the initiative began in 2020 by bringing Morningstar Investment Management together with Office and ByAllAccounts to enhance practice management workflows.

investor_qa.quote: By launching Morningstar Wealth Management with the combined solution-set of Morningstar Managed Portfolios, Morningstar Office, ByAllAccounts, and Morningstar.com we feel we are doing just that. Candidly, we’ve talked about doing this internally for a while now. In 2020, we began executing this initiative by bringing Morningstar Investment Management together with Office and ByAllAccounts to enhance practice management workflows so that advisors could increase their focus on delivering great financial advice.

value.topic: Direct exposure to Russia, Ukraine, and China; operations and vendor relationships
value.stated_position: Existing sales in Russia are immaterial and no clients in Ukraine; "We have recently stopped delivery of most services to Russian clients." A long-standing third-party vendor in Ukraine provides contract labor supporting PitchBook development and is considered "an important part of the Morningstar group," with the company working to provide financial help. External sales in China are not material; operations there "primarily support our global business," with a substantial number of employees in a data and technology development center in Shenzhen.

investor_qa.quote: Our existing sales in Russia are immaterial to the overall business and we currently do not have any clients procuring our products or services in Ukraine. We have recently stopped delivery of most services to Russian clients. We do have a long-standing relationship with a third-party vendor in Ukraine which provides contract labor in support of development efforts at PitchBook and consider them an important part of the Morningstar group.

value.topic: Integration of Sustainalytics ESG research across the business and ESG market opportunity
value.stated_position: Management states the overall objective is "to establish leading ESG positions across our business areas," pulling ESG data and research across Morningstar, with particular focus on enabling ESG adoption in the wealth space; direct indexing for advisors will feature Sustainalytics data at its core, and indexes/software offerings now carry ESG Risk Ratings. Market size estimates range from several hundred million to several billion dollars, suggesting the market "hasn't yet been consistently defined."

investor_qa.quote: While we are pleased with the performance of Sustainalytics, our overall objective is to establish leading ESG positions across our business areas, and we are making good progress in pulling through ESG-related data and research across Morningstar. We are particularly focused on enabling the adoption and implementation of ESG in the wealth space as we believe that doing so unlocks new personalization and impact tools for advisors and individuals.

value.topic: PitchBook growth drivers and total addressable market
value.stated_position: Growth comes from three main drivers: increasing the core customer user base, expansion into "adjacent" customer segments, and innovation and product upgrades. Over half of 2021 growth was from new sales, but management expects the proportion of growth from existing clients to increase over time. TAM estimated at $3.5 billion globally, consistent with prior disclosure, based on use-case assumptions.

investor_qa.quote: Our growth continues to come from three main drivers: Increasing the core customer user base (i.e., private equity and venture capital firms and institutional investors), increasing the user base through “adjacent” customer segments (i.e., corporate M&A teams, investment banks, and service providers), and innovation and product upgrades that add value and allow customers to use PitchBook more often to meet their needs.

value.topic: Morningstar Indexes growth drivers and long-term opportunity; competitive position versus entrenched index providers
value.stated_position: New client wins were the largest contributing factor, including a large client that converted from MSCI. Longer term the same factors should contribute, particularly in ESG, thematics, and private equity. Management characterises the index licensed data market as "ripe for disruption," with industry consolidation causing increased pricing by entrenched competitors and pushing clients to alternatives.

investor_qa.quote: In addition to expanded opportunities in AUM-linked revenue, we believe that the market for Index licensed data continues to be ripe for disruption. Industry consolidation has resulted in increased pricing by entrenched competitors leading clients to look for alternatives. In fact, in 2021, licensed data was the fastest growing part of our indexes business, and we expect that to continue.

value.topic: Employee turnover and initiatives to reduce attrition
value.stated_position: Attrition rose across all regions and business lines, consistent with most industries; management describes three key initiatives: re-engineering the exit interview process, greater investment in base compensation increases in 2021 and 2022 versus 2020, and investing in internal career mobility.

investor_qa.quote: We have three key initiatives underway to bring attrition down. First, we re-engineered our exit interview process to gain better insights into why people are leaving. We are using that information to inform our countermeasures. Second, we invested much more in base compensation increases in 2021 and 2022 compared with 2020. Third, we are investing in improving internal career mobility opportunities for our people.

value.topic: Advisor Workstation client decline and product direction
value.stated_position: The client decline was primarily a result of industry consolidation, and management says "we are not immune to M&A activity in the wealth management sector" given its enterprise client base; it maintained relationships with nearly all newly combined organizations. Product enhancements center on personalization (risk tolerance, risk capacity, ESG preferences), a modernized user experience, and capabilities like financial planning and compliance/regulatory needs in the US and Canada.

investor_qa.quote: The decline in clients for Advisor Workstation was primarily a result of industry consolidation. Given the number of enterprise clients that we serve, we are not immune to M&A activity in the wealth management sector. Despite this activity, we maintained relationships with nearly all of the newly combined organizations and continued to see strong trends in users across our client base.

value.topic: Capturing share of the RIA advisor market and evolving advisor-facing solutions
value.stated_position: Management says advisor-facing solutions "must evolve" as the RIA value proposition shifts toward personalization, financial planning, behavioral coaching, wellness, and tax planning, and that Morningstar is "fully engaging here across our solutions," including UMA functionality, embedding the Risk Ecosystem in Morningstar Office, embedding sustainability offerings across all advisor-facing products, models, and a proprietary direct indexing pilot beginning in Q2 2022 with a select group of financial advisors.

investor_qa.quote: As the value proposition of independent RIAs continues to shift toward areas like personalization, financial planning, behavioral coaching, wellness, and tax planning, advisor-facing solutions must evolve with respect to core portfolio management activities as well as these new areas of focus. We are fully engaging here across our solutions, integrating existing capabilities and developing new capabilities to address the changing needs of the investors they serve.

value.topic: Creation of the Morningstar Wealth Management product grouping under Daniel Needham
value.stated_position: Management describes uniting Managed Portfolios, Morningstar Office, ByAllAccounts, and Morningstar.com into a wealth management solutions product grouping, with the pending Praemium U.K./international acquisition also sitting within this group; the aim is "not" merely more advisors but "increasing the connectivity of our advisor solutions and increasing revenue per advisor."

investor_qa.quote: While adding more advisors is important, our aim is to continue increasing the connectivity of our advisor solutions and increasing revenue per advisor as a result.

value.topic: Competitive position of Morningstar's TAMP versus Envestnet and other larger TAMPs
value.stated_position: Management believes its platform "is at parity with or exceeds the experience offered by many of our competitors," continues to invest, and cites being voted the number-one TAMP by advisors for service and performance in The Wealth Advisor's America's Best TAMPs, 2022 edition.

investor_qa.quote: We believe our platform is at parity with or exceeds the experience offered by many of our competitors, and we continue to invest to enhance the experience.

value.topic: Differentiation of personalized portfolios; proprietary data sets
value.stated_position: Management points to independent research, proprietary data, and technology platforms, citing a proprietary direct indexing solution launching in beta in Q2 2022 combining Morningstar Sustainalytics metrics and Morningstar Indexes, and a new Target Date Plus service with Capital Group described as "a significant leap forward in the personalization of target-date funds."

investor_qa.quote: We believe this is a significant leap forward in the personalization of target-date funds and will be appealing to investors.

value.topic: Operating leverage and margins in the asset-based/Investment Management business
value.stated_position: Management declines to provide forward guidance on margins but says it is experiencing positive operating leverage as products attract assets, excluding the impact of "the disclosed client losses that were a result of our strategy shift," and is focusing on growing AUM.

investor_qa.quote: While we cannot provide forward guidance on margins, we are experiencing positive operating leverage as our products and investment strategies within Investment Management attract assets. That was indeed the case last year within Managed Portfolios, if we exclude the impact of the disclosed client losses that were a result of our strategy shift.

value.topic: Loss of the TD Ameritrade relationship and remaining large Investment Management contracts
value.stated_position: Management states the Managed Portfolios asset decrease from $48.6 billion in Q4 2019 to $23.1 billion in Q1 2020 is largely explained by the TD Ameritrade client loss, that TD Ameritrade switched to a fixed-fee arrangement as it transitioned the business in house and terminated the agreement following its merger with Charles Schwab, and that there are no remaining $10 million-plus clients in Investment Management revenue "as we shift away from consulting work to focus on direct relationships with advisors."

investor_qa.quote: There are no $10 million-plus clients contributing to Investment Management revenue as we shift away from consulting work to focus on direct relationships with advisors.

value.topic: Moving upmarket in Workplace/retirement plan managed accounts
value.stated_position: Management says small and midsize plans have "traditionally been the sweet spot" but it has built out a direct-to-plan sales team for larger plans, a consultant relations team, a specialized engagement team, and is building a call center; it says the investment "has started to pay off," citing Raytheon as its most recent large plan win.

investor_qa.quote: The small and midsize plan market has traditionally been the sweet spot for our managed accounts service. However, in the past few years we have built out the infrastructure to better serve and support larger plans.

value.topic: Adoption of managed accounts as a QDIA
value.stated_position: Management concedes it is "gaining traction and seeing increased interest but have not yet seen significant adoption" of managed accounts as a default option, particularly where recordkeepers have proprietary target-date funds they are encouraged to sell.

investor_qa.quote: We are gaining traction and seeing increased interest but have not yet seen significant adoption of managed accounts as a default option in the plans we work with, especially when distributed by recordkeepers that that have proprietary target-date funds that they are encouraged to sell to plans.

value.topic: Disclosure of Indexes revenue and possible reclassification of licensed data revenue
value.stated_position: Management says Indexes revenue is not disclosed separately "as it has not reached the size of our 'top' product categories," confirms the investor's derivation is "within a reasonable range," and says it will consider reclassifying licensed data product revenue within Indexes to the licensed-based category in the future.

investor_qa.quote: We do not currently disclose the Index revenue separately as it has not reached the size of our "top" product categories, but your derivation of Index revenue is within a reasonable range.

value.topic: Justification for the price paid for Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD)
value.stated_position: Management says it focuses on overall cash returns and expects the acquisition "to generate strong returns well above our cost of capital," plans to enhance a core product that "hasn't been updated in years" and sell it to PitchBook clients, and notes the divestiture was triggered by regulatory requirements from S&P Global's IHS Markit merger; on competitiveness of the process it says "While the process was likely competitive, we ran our own race."

investor_qa.quote: Through our extensive diligence and evaluation of how we will integrate LCD into Morningstar, we expect the acquisition to generate strong returns well above our cost of capital. We have significant opportunity to grow the product.

value.topic: LCD growth profile, accretion, and planned investment
value.stated_position: Management states LCD has experienced steady mid- to high-single-digit revenue growth, supported by "differentiated, hard-to-find data," that the transaction is expected to be accretive to adjusted net income per share in the first year after closing and to adjusted operating margins, and that it plans to invest behind the acquisition with much of that focused on integration into the PitchBook platform.

investor_qa.quote: We have plans to invest behind the acquisition to support future growth, with much of that focused on integration into the PitchBook platform. We expect our integration efforts to include more substantial product development activity and greater emphasis and resources to expand the go-to-market approach.

value.topic: Expected synergies from LCD across PitchBook, Indexes, and DBRS Morningstar
value.stated_position: Management declines to quantify but says there are "significant opportunities" particularly within PitchBook and Indexes that were factored into expected returns, including better penetration of the addressable market, new investable products based on LCD data, cross-selling, and support for DBRS Morningstar credit analysts.

investor_qa.quote: We believe there are significant opportunities across our business, particularly within PitchBook and Indexes, that were factored into our analysis and expected returns from the transaction.

value.topic: Margin pressure and willingness to invest ahead of growth; strategic priorities
value.stated_position: Management said it is "intent on balancing short- and long-term tradeoffs which can impact margins in periods of heavier investment," that this is the case today, and identified key strategic priorities as "delivering insights to public and private market investors, growing our ESG leadership position, capitalizing on wealth segment opportunities and scaling to support growth."

investor_qa.quote: As we often say, we are intent on balancing short- and long-term tradeoffs which can impact margins in periods of heavier investment. That is the case today, as we continue to have opportunities to deliver outsized revenue growth in the large and expanding addressable markets in which we serve investors. Our key strategic priorities include delivering insights to public and private market investors, growing our ESG leadership position, capitalizing on wealth segment opportunities and scaling to support growth.

value.topic: Stock-based compensation philosophy versus peers and whether it will converge
value.stated_position: Management defended stock awards as "an important part of our compensation philosophy to reward and incentivize our team members and align with our value creation objectives over time" and an important tool for attracting talent against fintech competitors; it declined to forecast convergence with peer metrics, saying it would not speculate on others' practices, and said awards will continue to be used "prudently."

investor_qa.quote: We cannot forecast convergence of metrics as we would not want to speculate on the objectives and compensation practices of others. Stock awards will continue to be an important part of our compensation structure and we will utilize them prudently to ensure they continue to achieve their intended purpose in incentivizing our team members.

value.topic: Employee attrition and retention initiatives
value.stated_position: Management disclosed attrition rose from 12.0% in 2020 to 18.5% in 2021 (vs a 2017-2019 average of 16.6% considered "more normalized") and described three initiatives: re-engineering the exit interview process, more investment in base compensation increases, and "investing in improving internal career mobility opportunities for our people" via a "more robust internal career marketplace."

investor_qa.quote: We have three initiatives underway focused on bringing attrition back to a more normalized number. First, we re-engineered our exit interview process to gain better insights into why people are leaving. We are using that information to inform our countermeasures. Second, we invested more in base compensation increases in 2021 and 2022 compared with 2020. Third, we are investing in improving internal career mobility opportunities for our people.

value.topic: Where headcount is concentrated across product areas
value.stated_position: Management declined to give workforce levels by product but stated: "Across our product areas and functions, the largest concentrations of headcount are currently in PitchBook, Morningstar Sustainalytics, our Wealth product areas, Data and Direct, and DBRS Morningstar," supported by large research and data collection teams, and acknowledged "we are investing more heavily in recent periods, given our higher rates of headcount growth relative to our peers."

investor_qa.quote: Across our product areas and functions, the largest concentrations of headcount are currently in PitchBook, Morningstar Sustainalytics, our Wealth product areas, Data and Direct, and DBRS Morningstar. Additionally, supporting these products and other areas are large teams within our research and data collection functions.

value.topic: Industry consolidation and whether Morningstar has the scale to compete
value.stated_position: Management said consolidation "creates both challenges and opportunities," that it is "often excited when larger competitors are distracted by large integrations," that "insights are not fungible" and investors value Morningstar's unique perspective, and that it will continue to invest in differentiated data sets; it expects added scale in credit ratings and wealth management "should be a positive for margins."

investor_qa.quote: In terms of scale, our growth suggests we are having success competing with larger firms. We believe insights are not fungible and investors value Morningstar’s unique perspective and the tools we provide to enable their workflows. As we have since the company was founded, we will continue to invest in and expand our differentiated data sets and analytics to meet evolving investor needs.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar competitive position and investment in corporate ratings
value.stated_position: Management said DBRS Morningstar "currently has limited presence in the leveraged finance sector (bank loans and CLOs) and the U.S. investment grade corporate market," that "We are investing to grow our corporate presence in both the U.S. and Europe," and attributed share gains to "quality of our ratings and our quick and efficient responsiveness to market participants that surpasses some of our competitors."

investor_qa.quote: DBRS Morningstar currently has limited presence in the leveraged finance sector (bank loans and CLOs) and the U.S. investment grade corporate market. That can help our relative growth rate in periods of market volatility and negatively impact the comparisons in periods of significant corporate issuance. We are investing to grow our corporate presence in both the U.S. and Europe.

value.topic: Disclosure practices — profitability by line of business
value.stated_position: Management said it continually evaluates disclosures and appreciates suggestions but "we do not anticipate disclosing our profitability by line of business," while noting it may consider replicating the directional margin analysis given at the 2020 Annual Meeting.

investor_qa.quote: We continually evaluate our disclosures and what information could be useful to our shareholders and appreciate the suggestions you are making although we do not anticipate disclosing our profitability by line of business.

value.topic: Adjusted EBITDA as used for executive bonus purposes
value.stated_position: Management explained that its Adjusted EBITDA measures the business on a "pre-bonus" basis, excluding the large variable incentive compensation component, and that it is "an annual measurement used solely for bonus purposes and is reviewed and approved annually by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors."

investor_qa.quote: We do not calculate Adjusted EBITDA quarterly as it is an annual measurement used solely for bonus purposes and is reviewed and approved annually by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors.

value.topic: Long-term profitability targets and investment priorities
value.stated_position: Management confirmed it is "investing heavily in the business, reflecting the opportunities we see to deliver outsized revenue growth in the large and expanding addressable markets in which we serve investors," naming Pitchbook, DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar Sustainalytics, Indexes, and Wealth Management as the largest investment areas, and said that while it does not disclose long-term margin targets, "our goal is to improve margins over time as we scale and benefit from operating leverage."

investor_qa.quote: While we do not disclose our long-term margin targets, our goal is to improve margins over time as we scale and benefit from operating leverage and the investments we are making in the business.

value.topic: Sustainalytics differentiation and value proposition
value.stated_position: Management said its key differentiator is the ability "to inform investors throughout the investment lifecycle from pre-investment analysis and screens, through the investment decision itself, to the post-investment stage," and pointed to the ESG Risk Rating's "focus on absolute rather than relative risk," the EU Action Plan solution set, and "our large and responsive customer service organization."

investor_qa.quote: We believe that one of our key differentiators and an important part of our value proposition is our ability to inform investors throughout the investment lifecycle from pre-investment analysis and screens, through the investment decision itself, to the post-investment stage, when our data helps clients vote on shareholder resolutions and engage with companies in their portfolios.

value.topic: New climate ratings planned for late 2022
value.stated_position: Management stated it continues to invest in new data and analytics "with a recent focus on climate and impact data" and will debut new physical risk and transition risk ratings in late 2022.

investor_qa.quote: In late 2022, we will debut new ratings that help investors more directly understand how the changing climate could affect a company (physical risk) and how a company is adapting to the shift toward a low-carbon economy (transition risk).

value.topic: Growth drivers and target customers for Sustainalytics
value.stated_position: Asset managers and asset owners account for the largest share of Sustainalytics revenue; growth drivers cited are "the evolving global regulatory environment as well as the opportunity to expand our penetration within large asset managers and to reach more middle market clients, especially in the United States," plus corporate licensed ratings and second-party opinions for green and sustainability bonds.

investor_qa.quote: Growth drivers include the evolving global regulatory environment as well as the opportunity to expand our penetration within large asset managers and to reach more middle market clients, especially in the United States.

value.topic: Competitive position in green bond verification
value.stated_position: Management cited being named by the Climate Bonds Initiative as "the Largest Verifier for Certified Climate Bonds for a fifth consecutive year" and described a "strong competitive position" in second-party opinions for green and sustainability bonds.

investor_qa.quote: In June 2022, the Climate Bonds Initiative (CBI) named Morningstar Sustainalytics the Largest Verifier for Certified Climate Bonds for a fifth consecutive year, while noting that in 2021 the market for green bonds nearly doubled in volume to more than USD 1.1 trillion compared to 2020.

value.topic: Firm-wide ESG objective
value.stated_position: Management stated the "overall objective is to establish leading ESG positions across Morningstar," leveraging Sustainalytics data, research, and ratings across products including direct indexing for advisors and a new Sustainability hub in Direct.

investor_qa.quote: More broadly, our overall objective is to establish leading ESG positions across Morningstar. We are leveraging Sustainalytics data, research, and ratings to meet that goal.

value.topic: PitchBook addressable market and penetration
value.stated_position: Management stated the total addressable market for PitchBook is 114,000 firms against 8,000 firms served today, leaving "considerable room for growth, especially as we integrate the capabilities of our recently acquired Leveraged Commentary & Data product area."

investor_qa.quote: As we discussed at our Annual Shareholder Meeting, we view the total addressable market for PitchBook to be 114,000 firms. We serve 8,000 firms today.

value.topic: ESG assessment of private companies
value.stated_position: Management said Sustainalytics offers a pre-IPO ESG assessment service but "does not otherwise proactively rate private companies at this time," and is evaluating opportunities to expand ESG assessments to private companies.

investor_qa.quote: Morningstar Sustainalytics does offer a pre-IPO ESG assessment service for private companies but does not otherwise proactively rate private companies at this time. We are evaluating opportunities to expand our ESG assessments to private companies.

value.topic: Prioritizing topline growth versus margin expansion
value.stated_position: "We are prioritizing our investments in areas of the business where we see the opportunity to grow, build scale, and generate attractive long-term returns" and while these investments "can put pressure on margins in the short-term," management does "not anticipate that they will come at the expense of long-term returns or future margin expansion." No guidance on specific revenue or margin targets.

investor_qa.quote: We are prioritizing our investments in areas of the business where we see the opportunity to grow, build scale, and generate attractive long-term returns. We know that these investments can put pressure on margins in the short-term, but we do not anticipate that they will come at the expense of long-term returns or future margin expansion.

value.topic: Areas of heaviest investment within license-based products
value.stated_position: Within license-based products, "we are investing particularly heavily in PitchBook and Sustainalytics"; DBRS Morningstar is described as "an area of significant investment"; Investment Management and Index areas have lower margins "reflecting the significant investment we are making to drive growth and scale," with a goal to "grow AUM and our revenue per advisor over time."

investor_qa.quote: Notably, as we build important capabilities in Wealth (including in direct indexing and our TAMP), our goal is to grow AUM and our revenue per advisor over time.

value.topic: Pace of hiring given inflation and peers slowing investment
value.stated_position: "We take a long-term view of our investment priorities, including spending on increased headcount," but management "acknowledge certain challenges in the current economic environment" and is taking them into consideration "including around the pace of hiring," promising to "be prudent and will adjust as necessary."

investor_qa.quote: That said, we acknowledge certain challenges in the current economic environment and are taking these into consideration as we make spending decisions, including around the pace of hiring. We will continue to be prudent and will adjust as necessary to balance our long-term priorities against changes in market conditions.

value.topic: Whether there is a structural limit to growth versus data/analytics peers
value.stated_position: "We don't see any structural limits to growth." Many products, including in Wealth, Indexes and DBRS Morningstar, "do not yet have the scale that our competitors enjoy." DBRS's $271 million of 2021 revenue is contrasted with $3.8 billion for Moody's Investor Services and $4.1 billion for S&P's Ratings segment, whose "size and market share in the US investment-grade corporate market create significant operating leverage."

investor_qa.quote: We don’t see any structural limits to growth. The headcount increases you reference and the impact on revenue per employee reflect the significant investments we are making in parts of the business where we see attractive opportunities to grow, achieve scale, and generate attractive long-term returns. These areas are growing rapidly and many products, including in Wealth, Indexes and DBRS Morningstar, do not yet have the scale that our competitors enjoy.

value.topic: Near-term capital allocation priorities and willingness to use debt
value.stated_position: "We continue to take a balanced approach to capital allocation with a primary emphasis on organic opportunities to drive growth," retaining flexibility to be opportunistic on M&A; returning cash to shareholders is "a key component of our capital deployment," with $111 million repurchased in Q1 2022. Management remains "open using the private placement market in the future."

investor_qa.quote: We continue to take a balanced approach to capital allocation with a primary emphasis on organic opportunities to drive growth. That said, we’ve retained flexibility over the years to be opportunistic and pursue M&A opportunities that support our growth strategies.

value.topic: Leverage tolerance following the LCD acquisition
value.stated_position: Leverage increased to 2.3x Debt/EBITDA on a proforma basis, a level management believes "is manageable to operate the business and continue to pursue our capital allocation priorities"; the credit agreement caps leverage at 3.75x in the event of an acquisition, and management will "continue to make sure we are prudent with a focus on maintaining a strong balance sheet."

investor_qa.quote: We believe that level is manageable to operate the business and continue to pursue our capital allocation priorities. In the past we have increased our debt position and taken leverage levels up to pursue acquisitions (notably with PitchBook and DBRS). It's worth noting that our current credit agreement caps our leverage at 3.75x Debt/EBITDA in the event of an acquisition.

value.topic: Use of international cash
value.stated_position: "Bringing cash to the U.S. often triggers adverse tax consequences," but the company has worked to minimize the offshore balance "through efficient repatriation activities and strategic opportunities," citing the final Sustainalytics purchase consideration payment funded fully with overseas cash.

investor_qa.quote: Bringing cash to the U.S. often triggers adverse tax consequences, but we have worked to minimize that balance over time through efficient repatriation activities and strategic opportunities. As an example, we recently completed the final cash payment of the purchase consideration for Sustainalytics by fully funding that commitment with overseas cash.

value.topic: Integration approach for Sustainalytics, PitchBook/LCD and DBRS
value.stated_position: "Every transaction we do has a unique integration plan which is tailored to the capabilities we are acquiring and the strategy we are pursuing." DBRS focus was "combining our U.S. methodologies and operations"; Sustainalytics ESG research is being leveraged across products; "our plan is to integrate LCD into the PitchBook platform to complement the private market data that exists within it today."

investor_qa.quote: Every transaction we do has a unique integration plan which is tailored to the capabilities we are acquiring and the strategy we are pursuing. The degree of integration differs depending on the capability.

value.topic: Cloud transition
value.stated_position: "Morningstar, like many companies, is in the midst of its cloud transition," migrating on-premise data centers to the cloud; over time management expects "lower capital expenditures for physical hardware and higher operating expenses in certain areas for cloud computing capacity." New product development is "focused on leveraging cloud native services."

investor_qa.quote: Morningstar, like many companies, is in the midst of its cloud transition. That includes migrating our on-premise data centers to the cloud and building new products and capabilities in that environment. Over time, we expect that migration to translate to lower capital expenditures for physical hardware and higher operating expenses in certain areas for cloud computing capacity.

value.topic: Client mix strategy — institutional asset managers and corporates
value.stated_position: Management sees "good growth prospects for Sustainalytics and Indexes" within institutional asset managers; in the corporate market it enjoys "a leading position in the second opinion provider business"; DBRS Morningstar is leveraging global investor relationships and central bank acceptance of its ratings to grow corporate ratings in Europe and "in the US it is making an entry in the middle market private corporate market."

investor_qa.quote: Meanwhile, DBRS Morningstar is leveraging our relationships with global investors and the accepted use of its credit ratings by central banks to drive growth in corporate ratings in Europe; in the US it is making an entry in the middle market private corporate market.

value.topic: Cyclicality of DBRS Morningstar
value.stated_position: Roughly two-thirds of 2021 DBRS revenue came from structured finance; in the US and Europe "we are more susceptible to interest-rate volatility and issuance volumes in that segment." Management states "our profile is very different today than it was back in 2008," with a business "approaching $300 million in revenue" that is "more diverse across asset classes and geography, with a larger recurring-revenue base."

investor_qa.quote: While we are not immune to cyclicality and the impacts of market volatility in credit ratings, our profile is very different today than it was back in 2008. Today, DBRS Morningstar operates a business approaching $300 million in revenue and is more diverse across asset classes and geography, with a larger recurring-revenue base.

value.topic: PitchBook's competitive position in a recessionary environment
value.stated_position: "we are confident in our ability to provide value to clients regardless of market environment"; if clients consolidate research solutions, "we are confident that our data, product, and service will stack up well against any other provider, regardless of relative cost."

investor_qa.quote: In the event that clients want to consolidate their research solutions, we are confident that our data, product, and service will stack up well against any other provider, regardless of relative cost.

value.topic: PitchBook TAM increase to $4.9bn
value.stated_position: Methodology "has remained consistent with the methodology we disclosed in 2021"; as PitchBook added data and capabilities it met more client use cases, and "the count of firms in PitchBook's TAM grew by 26% as of our 2022 estimate, driven primarily by the companies and core client segment."

investor_qa.quote: Our methodology for sizing PitchBook’s total addressable market (TAM) has remained consistent with the methodology we disclosed in 2021. To be included in the TAM, a firm must be active in at least one use case that PitchBook supports (three use cases for our companies client segment).

value.topic: Measuring Wealth Management and direct indexing investment
value.stated_position: Investments across the US TAMP, Morningstar Wealth Platform, Morningstar Office, ByAllAccounts and Morningstar Investor "will allow us to serve a broader base of advisors and investors, driving license- and asset-based fees"; direct indexing is expected "to be a key driver of AUM growth" and the focus is "increasing assets and our revenue per advisor over time."

investor_qa.quote: We believe these investments will allow us to serve a broader base of advisors and investors, driving license- and asset-based fees from these products. This includes direct indexing, which we expect to be a key driver of AUM growth.

value.topic: Rationale for investing in SMArtX
value.stated_position: "SMArtX has a track record of building products that offer flexibility, advisor choice and personalization at scale, which aligns with our mission of empowering investor success"; its technology platform "will be integral to delivering a larger selection of investment offerings through Morningstar's TAMP."

investor_qa.quote: SMArtX has a track record of building products that offer flexibility, advisor choice and personalization at scale, which aligns with our mission of empowering investor success and the demands of advisors. SMArtX’s technology platform will be integral to delivering a larger selection of investment offerings through Morningstar’s TAMP and we’ll be sharing more details about this in the second half of the year.

value.topic: Backlash over the Morningstar Investor portfolio rewrite
value.stated_position: Management is "excited about the June launch of Morningstar Investor," acknowledges feedback "largely been focused on gaps in features, which the team is actively working to close," says legacy portfolio tools "continue to be accessible and will remain so for several months," and reports "a brief spike in cancellations in our weekly metrics which has since reverted to normal levels" with "minimal impact to net subscription numbers and revenue for this product."

investor_qa.quote: We saw a brief spike in cancellations in our weekly metrics which has since reverted to normal levels. Subscriptions to Investor have run at a slightly higher rate relative to the pre-launch period. Taken together, we have seen minimal impact to net subscription numbers and revenue for this product.

value.topic: Investment priorities and timing of returns on investment spending
value.stated_position: "This year, our investment priorities include Wealth, ESG / Morningstar Sustainalytics, and PitchBook in addition to addressing key infrastructure needs to help us scale." Management said it cannot guide to a specific inflection point in profitability, expects adjusted operating margins this year to be lower than a typical year, and is "focused on getting back on a path toward levels seen in recent historical peaks," noting different time horizons for returns \u2014 shorter-term for Morningstar Sustainalytics and PitchBook, longer for Wealth (direct indexing and open architecture TAMP expansion).

investor_qa.quote: As we noted in our annual meeting earlier this year, we are investing in key areas of the business to address market opportunities. This year, our investment priorities include Wealth, ESG / Morningstar Sustainalytics, and PitchBook in addition to addressing key infrastructure needs to help us scale.

value.topic: Sales and marketing spending discipline and operating leverage
value.stated_position: "We believe that as we grow, we will have the opportunity to generate operating leverage in our sales and marketing activities. That said, we will continue to spend prudently in sales and marketing activities where we see the potential to generate attractive returns, which could result in higher levels of spend in certain periods."

investor_qa.quote: We believe that as we grow, we will have the opportunity to generate operating leverage in our sales and marketing activities. That said, we will continue to spend prudently in sales and marketing activities where we see the potential to generate attractive returns, which could result in higher levels of spend in certain periods.

value.topic: Restructuring of China operations
value.stated_position: Morningstar "made the decision to strategically shift our China operations to focus entirely on the China domestic market," requiring it to "streamline the team in Shenzhen accordingly over the next 12 months." Non-China-market-focused work is being shifted to alternate locations, "so this decision is not a cost-savings measure," and Morningstar "remains committed to its long-term presence and is in the process of redefining its strategy to capitalize on the growing potential within the domestic market."

investor_qa.quote: After careful consideration, we have made the decision to strategically shift our China operations to focus entirely on the China domestic market. This requires us to streamline the team in Shenzhen accordingly over the next 12 months.

value.topic: Increased appetite for large M&A and how acquisitions fit the existing business
value.stated_position: "When it comes to capital allocation, our primary emphasis is supporting organic growth; however, we will continue to pursue acquisitions opportunistically." Over the past 10 years it completed 39 transactions; growing scale, profitability and cash flow "expanded our capacity to do larger cash and debt-financed transactions," and it has "tended to focus on larger acquisitions, which have a more substantial impact." But "we do not pursue M&A simply because we have the capacity to do so; all transactions need to have strategic merit, offer compelling long-term returns, and create value." Each of the four largest deals since end-2016 (PitchBook, DBRS, Sustainalytics, LCD) strengthened the existing business.

investor_qa.quote: When it comes to capital allocation, our primary emphasis is supporting organic growth; however, we will continue to pursue acquisitions opportunistically where we identify opportunities that enhance our ability to empower investor success and create value for shareholders.

value.topic: Independent investigation into Morningstar Sustainalytics' research practices and alleged anti-Israel bias
value.stated_position: "neither Morningstar nor Morningstar Sustainalytics supports the anti-Israel BDS campaign. However, in retrospect, our initial review was overly dismissive of the serious bias concerns raised by the organization JLens, the Illinois Investment Policy Board (IIPB), and other entities." A working group led by independent directors Steve Kaplan and Gail Landis engaged White & Case in October 2021; the 117-page report found no evidence of pervasive or systemic bias but identified one product that exhibited bias in its outcomes; Morningstar "committed to adopt in full" the recommendations and plans to complete implementation by June 2023.

investor_qa.quote: However, in retrospect, our initial review was overly dismissive of the serious bias concerns raised by the organization JLens, the Illinois Investment Policy Board (IIPB), and other entities. We consider bias unacceptable in any form and concluded that the concerns warranted a thorough, independent review.

value.topic: Joe Mansueto's pledged shares and new pledging policy
value.stated_position: As of December 31, 2021 Joe Mansueto had pledged 1,800,000 shares as security under a bank credit agreement, down from 3,000,000 a year earlier, representing about 10% of his beneficially owned shares and 4% of total shares outstanding; the pledge "was arranged to provide Joe some opportunity to diversify his assets, consistent with the advice Morningstar often gives investors." Effective July 2022 the Code of Ethics was amended to prohibit pledging more than 15% of beneficially owned Morningstar securities, with Audit Committee review; the Audit Committee determined Joe's arrangements "do not present a significant risk of a margin call or subsequent foreclosure sale."

investor_qa.quote: Effective July 2022, Morningstar has amended its Code of Ethics to prohibit employees and board members from pledging more than 15% of the total number of Morningstar securities (such as shares of Morningstar stock) which they beneficially own as collateral for a loan or holding more than that number of Morningstar securities in a margin account.

value.topic: Return on capital in M&A and the price paid for the LCD acquisition
value.stated_position: "We evaluate the returns of any potential M&A transaction relative to expected returns for other uses of capital. In determining the price we pay for acquisitions, we focus on cash-on-cash returns and internal rates of return." For LCD, management said low historical investment was insufficient to realize its "significant growth potential, especially given secular tailwinds for private credit," and that it is "confident in our ability to realize value and excess returns as we invest in the integration."

investor_qa.quote: We evaluate the returns of any potential M&A transaction relative to expected returns for other uses of capital. In determining the price we pay for acquisitions, we focus on cash-on-cash returns and internal rates of return. Our acquisition planning is informed by comprehensive diligence and the value we expect to deliver through integrating acquisitions into our business.

value.topic: Confidence that profitability will recover and improve after margin erosion
value.stated_position: Management restated its position that "there is inherent leverage in the business" and that current investments will drive long-term returns and margin improvement, naming "Morningstar Sustainalytics, Wealth, and PitchBook" as the key opportunity areas; returns in Sustainalytics climate/impact metrics and PitchBook equity data are expected to materialize more quickly, while Wealth (direct indexing, open architecture TAMP) "will take more time to materialize."

investor_qa.quote: As we’ve stated previously, we believe that there is inherent leverage in the business and that the investments that we’re making will help drive attractive long-term returns and margin improvements. We are focused on growth and scale and shared some of those comparisons at our 2022 annual meeting. We believe significant opportunity exists in key areas including Morningstar Sustainalytics, Wealth, and PitchBook.

value.topic: Changes to incentive compensation structure and merit increases
value.stated_position: The "most notable change in the 2022 compensation structure was the increase in our merit pool," roughly double the prior year's rate and "almost double the weighted average market rate across our global footprint as we were focused on retaining talent in a highly competitive environment." Additional compensation was invested in salaries and bonuses "to close the adjusted gender pay gap identified in a 2021 review," and in geographies/product areas with higher turnover (India, Morningstar Sustainalytics, DBRS Morningstar, PitchBook). Management is "keeping a careful eye on inflation globally in our approach to 2023."

investor_qa.quote: The most notable change in the 2022 compensation structure was the increase in our merit pool with a budgeted global weighted average percentage increase adjusted for headcount that was roughly double the rate in the prior year; we believe that the budgeted increase was also almost double the weighted average market rate across our global footprint as we were focused on retaining talent in a highly competitive environment.

value.topic: Decision to stop reporting certain KPIs (Direct/PitchBook licenses, Morningstar.com premium subscribers, Advisor Workstation clients)
value.stated_position: KPIs were moved to the Supplemental Deck; premium website subscriptions will be published annually rather than quarterly "as it does not rank among our top products"; and the company "made the recent decision to stop disclosing the number of Advisor Workstation clients," concluding "it was not as relevant a metric and not highly correlated to revenue given the heterogeneity of our client contracts."

investor_qa.quote: We also made the recent decision to stop disclosing the number of Advisor Workstation clients. We came to the conclusion that it was not as relevant a metric and not highly correlated to revenue given the heterogeneity of our client contracts, and specifically, the wide variation in advisor user counts and size from client to client.

value.topic: Why the company does not disclose more detail on investment spending at DBRS and PitchBook
value.stated_position: Management said it has "given directional guidelines on comparative margins within our portfolio" in the past and "will consider how we can better characterize and explain incremental investments going forward."

investor_qa.quote: In the past, we have given directional guidelines on comparative margins within our portfolio. In response to a related question published this month, we have provided more detail on investments we’re making in headcount in product areas targeted for growth. We will consider how we can better characterize and explain incremental investments going forward.

value.topic: Currency in which PitchBook and other license-based products are priced
value.stated_position: PitchBook contracts are priced in USD while other licensed-based products are "generally priced in the local market currency"; the company is "in the process of transitioning the pricing of PitchBook products to local currencies and expect to complete this project by the end of 2023."

investor_qa.quote: You are correct that PitchBook contracts are priced in USD. Our other licensed-based products are generally priced in the local market currency, with a few exceptions to accommodate client preferences. We are in the process of transitioning the pricing of PitchBook products to local currencies and expect to complete this project by the end of 2023.

value.topic: How hiring priorities have changed over time
value.stated_position: "At any given time, our hiring priorities reflect our strategic priorities." In 2022 there was greater focus on "Wealth, PitchBook, ESG/Morningstar Sustainalytics and DBRS Morningstar as well as on the infrastructure to help us scale," largely similar to 2021; the company hires "more heavily in years after acquisitions to drive our investment thesis and returns."

investor_qa.quote: At any given time, our hiring priorities reflect our strategic priorities. In 2022, there has been a greater focus on Wealth, PitchBook, ESG/Morningstar Sustainalytics and DBRS Morningstar as well as on the infrastructure to help us scale. Those priorities are largely similar to 2021. In many cases, we hire more heavily in years after acquisitions to drive our investment thesis and returns.

value.topic: Scale of investment in Morningstar Sustainalytics and expected pace ahead
value.stated_position: Management is "investing heavily in Morningstar Sustainalytics," hiring to expand research IP "particularly in the new areas of impact and climate," with new products to come to market in 2023; "The pace of Sustainalytics hiring is expected to slow in 2023." It states dollar costs are growing faster than organic revenues and that Sustainalytics' margins "are a drag on our overall margins," but are expected over time to reach levels in line with the licensed-based product group average.

investor_qa.quote: The pace of hiring to support these two new research capabilities was intensive in 2021 and 2022 as the business built up the expertise required to bring new impact and climate products to market in 2023. We also meaningfully invested to support the research needed to address clients’ compliance requirements related to the EU Action Plan regulation. The pace of Sustainalytics hiring is expected to slow in 2023.

value.topic: Implications of ESG regulation and political backlash, including state Attorneys General inquiries
value.stated_position: "We do not anticipate a material impact to Morningstar Sustainalytics or its clients from the recent inquiries initiated by the Attorney Generals of several U.S. states or more broadly from heightened scrutiny of ESG in the United States. If that were to change, we would disclose accordingly." Management frames Morningstar's role as providing "the independent data and insights that make those conversations more informed."

investor_qa.quote: We do not anticipate a material impact to Morningstar Sustainalytics or its clients from the recent inquiries initiated by the Attorney Generals of several U.S. states or more broadly from heightened scrutiny of ESG in the United States. If that were to change, we would disclose accordingly. There are differing views on the merits of sustainable investing, but global investor interest in it has become mainstream

value.topic: Comparison of Sustainalytics margins with MSCI's ESG & Climate segment
value.stated_position: Management declined the comparison — "We’re not familiar with the particulars of how MSCI handles its segment-level reporting" — while acknowledging Sustainalytics "currently has the lowest margins of our licensed-based products" and is expected over time to approach the others.

investor_qa.quote: We’re not familiar with the particulars of how MSCI handles its segment-level reporting, so it’s difficult for us to directly compare the profitability of MSCI’s ESG and Climate segment to Morningstar Sustainalytics’ margins. That said, given our substantial investments in Sustainalytics, that product group currently has the lowest margins of our licensed-based products.

value.topic: Plan for integrating LCD into PitchBook and Morningstar Indexes
value.stated_position: The plan is to "integrate Leveraged Commentary & Data ( LCD) data, analytics, and research with PitchBook’s to offer a consolidated workflow for public and private capital and debt market research," with LCD staff moved onto PitchBook teams; on the Indexes side, operations are transitioning from S&P to Morningstar, the LCD indexes have been renamed under the Morningstar brand, and the Indexes sales team has been trained on the suite.

investor_qa.quote: We plan to integrate Leveraged Commentary & Data ( LCD) data, analytics, and research with PitchBook’s to offer a consolidated workflow for public and private capital and debt market research. LCD datasets will enrich the overall PitchBook platform adding comprehensive coverage of leveraged loans, high-yield bonds, and more.

value.topic: Motivation for the LCD acquisition and target customer types
value.stated_position: The acquisition "was motivated by the value that we see in Leveraged Commentary & Data’s ( LCD) capabilities in private credit and leveraged loan data, research, and indexes against the backdrop of attractive secular tailwinds for private credit," and management has "confirmed the private credit use cases in our total addressable market (TAM)" after a full review of LCD's clients.

investor_qa.quote: The acquisition was motivated by the value that we see in Leveraged Commentary & Data’s ( LCD) capabilities in private credit and leveraged loan data, research, and indexes against the backdrop of attractive secular tailwinds for private credit. Adding LCD’s coverage to PitchBook’s institutional-grade coverage of the public and private equity markets creates a comprehensive data and research tool.

value.topic: Investment in the LCD product versus letting margin fall to the bottom line
value.stated_position: "As we manage through that process, we will invest to maximize long-term returns." PitchBook "plans to make important investments to improve the LCD product, the LCD data set within the PitchBook platform, and our support of LCD customers, which we believe will help to accelerate growth and enhance margins."

investor_qa.quote: As we integrate LCD into the business, PitchBook plans to make important investments to improve the LCD product, the LCD data set within the PitchBook platform, and our support of LCD customers, which we believe will help to accelerate growth and enhance margins.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar headcount strategy and strategic initiatives through the credit cycle
value.stated_position: The company continues "to invest in analytical and operations staff globally to maintain/defend the existing business, but more importantly to continue to grow the business globally," with initiatives in US middle market and European corporates, growing the data business, and technology investments for operational scalability. Given issuance volatility, "we manage our headcount by slowing hiring in times of lower issuance" but "don’t downsize or stop hiring completely."

investor_qa.quote: Given the volatility of credit issuance levels, we manage our headcount by slowing hiring in times of lower issuance and managing attrition accordingly. We don’t downsize or stop hiring completely since we need to be adequately staffed for when issuance volumes normalize/pick-up and we continue to invest in the business, consistent with our long-term growth plans.

value.topic: Approach to the public cloud migration and its cost profile
value.stated_position: Management said it does not have an R&D expense line and capitalizes software development costs, follows either a "lift and shift model" or an "optimize first" model, and does "not anticipate increased expenses to support two code bases" because cost duplication is short. Over time it expects "a decline in capex and related depreciation associated with the purchase and maintenance of on-premise servers and an increase in operating expenses related to our use of cloud services."

investor_qa.quote: Over time, as we continue our transition from on-premise servers to the cloud, we expect to see a decline in capex and related depreciation associated with the purchase and maintenance of on-premise servers and an increase in operating expenses related to our use of cloud services.

value.topic: Retention of LCD talent and onboarding
value.stated_position: "The onboarding process has been very successful, and we have seen minimal attrition." The company spent the first several months understanding roles and has begun transitioning the LCD reporting structure to the relevant PitchBook or Morningstar teams, adding resources in research, support, and account management.

investor_qa.quote: The onboarding process has been very successful, and we have seen minimal attrition. We took the first several months following the acquisition to fully understand the roles and responsibilities of the Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD) team.

value.topic: Investment spending and operating margin trajectory
value.stated_position: Management said a significant portion of recent operating expense growth is driven by investments to build capabilities to support growth in prioritized products — PitchBook, Morningstar Sustainalytics, and Wealth Management — and that it takes a long-term view while being "prudent with spending decisions given challenges in the economic environment," expecting margins this year to be lower than a typical year but focused on getting back toward recent historical peaks.

investor_qa.quote: As to the timing of investments, we take a long-term view and invest where we see attractive opportunities to grow, achieve scale, and generate strong long-term returns. We are also being prudent with spending decisions given challenges in the economic environment.  As we noted in our investor question responses published in August, while we expect that operating margins this year will be lower than in a typical year, we are focused on getting back on a path toward levels seen in recent historical peaks.

value.topic: LCD integration and which PitchBook client segments it will expand
value.stated_position: Management said the biggest opportunities from LCD's capabilities are with lenders, investors, banks and service providers and, to a lesser extent, limited partners, and that integrating LCD data into the PitchBook platform will expand reach with those segments.

investor_qa.quote: As we look at LCD’s capabilities, we see the biggest opportunities with lenders, investors, banks and service providers and, to a lesser extent, limited partners. We expect that the integration of LCD data and analysis into the PitchBook platform will expand our reach with those client segments.

value.topic: Conditions for the $50 million contingent LCD payment
value.stated_position: Management explained the $50 million contingent consideration, payable six months after the June 1, 2022 close, is contingent on transitioning LCD customer relationships — specifically unbundling LCD contracts from other S&P services into standalone Morningstar agreements — paid based on percentage of customer ACV successfully unbundled as of December 1, 2022.

investor_qa.quote: To encourage focus on this transition, the contingent consideration of up to $50 million will be paid based on the percentage of customer ACV that has been successfully unbundled as of December 1, 2022.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar's competitive position versus Moody's and S&P
value.stated_position: Management said growth was driven by U.S. CMBS ratings activity "where we enjoy a leading position," and that unlike Moody's and S&P, DBRS Morningstar currently has a smaller share of the U.S. corporate and CLO markets.

investor_qa.quote: Unlike Moody’s and S&P, DBRS Morningstar currently has a smaller share of the U.S. corporate and collateralized loan obligation (CLOs) markets, which saw steep declines in issuance.

value.topic: TAMP moving to open architecture with third-party models
value.stated_position: Management said demand is for flexibility and choice, with unified and separately managed accounts growing ahead of ETF and mutual fund models, and that "we plan to open our TAMP to third-party models in the coming months, migrating to an open architecture model."

investor_qa.quote: To meet the demand for flexibility, we plan to open our TAMP to third-party models in the coming months, migrating to an open architecture model.

value.topic: Direct indexing growth opportunity and competitive advantage
value.stated_position: Management called direct indexing "an attractive growth opportunity for Morningstar," said it believes Cerulli's projected 12.4% annual growth through 2026 is conservative, and located its competitive advantage in the breadth of capabilities and proprietary IP across Morningstar Indexes, Sustainalytics and Equity Research, brand strength with advisors, and the ability to bring all direct indexing components together in-house, with pricing generally in line with or lower than competitors.

investor_qa.quote: We stand out for our ability to bring all the direct indexing components together using in-house capabilities. Our pricing is generally in line with or lower than our competitors in this market.

value.topic: Purpose of share repurchases
value.stated_position: Management said it makes significant share repurchases when it believes the return potential is attractive compared to other uses of capital, and expressly not for the purpose of share-based compensation.

investor_qa.quote: We make significant share repurchases when we believe that the return potential is attractive compared to other uses of capital. We do not do so for the purpose of share-based compensation.

value.topic: Total price paid for Sustainalytics
value.stated_position: Management disclosed the acquisition of the remaining stake closed July 2, 2020, with three cash payments — an initial payment at closing plus earn-outs on June 30, 2021 and June 30, 2022 based on a multiple of Morningstar Sustainalytics' revenues — totalling EUR 147.1 million.

investor_qa.quote: The total consideration across the three payments was EUR 147.1 million.

value.topic: Gross margin versus peers and reliance on third-party data
value.stated_position: Management said it is "difficult to make direct comparisons with our peers' gross margins given differences in our business mix," that it does not believe its gross margin is capped, and that it does not believe it is more reliant on third-party datasets than peers or faces a higher cost of sourcing data.

investor_qa.quote: It is difficult to make direct comparisons with our peers’ gross margins given differences in our business mix. Importantly, we do not believe that our gross margin is capped, and we have invested to fund growth.

value.topic: Debt structure and funding of the LCD acquisition
value.stated_position: Management said the credit facility structure, particularly the term loan used for the LCD acquisition, "is a good fit for our needs," that its prepayable nature will allow excess cash to pay it down over time, that a similar funding strategy was used for DBRS, and that it does not currently swap out any of its debt.

investor_qa.quote: The structure of our credit facility, particularly the term loan component used for the LCD acquisition, is a good fit for our needs. The prepayable nature of the loan will allow us to use excess cash to pay it down over time. We were able to use a similar funding strategy with the acquisition of DBRS.

value.topic: Target leverage ratio and prioritization of debt repayment over share repurchases
value.stated_position: Management said it does not target a specific debt ratio but takes "a conservative approach to managing our balance sheet," describing a historical pattern of increasing debt for acquisitions (notably PitchBook and DBRS) then paying it down, and stated that "debt repayment will be a near-to-intermediate-term priority for deployment of excess cash."

investor_qa.quote: While we do not target a specific debt ratio, we do take a conservative approach to managing our balance sheet. Historically, we have increased our debt levels with a corresponding increase in our leverage ratio to pursue acquisitions (notably PitchBook and DBRS) and then paid down debt in subsequent periods.

value.topic: Senator Pat Toomey's request for information on Morningstar Sustainalytics research practices
value.stated_position: Management said it has responded and is answering follow-up questions, does not plan to make the response public at this time, continues to engage with legislators and other stakeholders, and will disclose any material outcome per legal/regulatory requirements or usual investor channels.

investor_qa.quote: We have responded to Senator Pat Toomey’s request for information and are in the process of answering follow-up questions related to that response. We do not plan to make the response public at this time.

value.topic: PitchBook management incentive compensation plan
value.stated_position: Management described the PitchBook incentive plan adopted with the acquisition for 2017-2019 and renewed at the end of 2019 for 2020-2022, with awards tied to revenue targets specific to PitchBook's business and higher target incentives in the third year of the plan.

investor_qa.quote: The PitchBook incentive plan, which we adopted in connection with the acquisition of PitchBook for the 2017-2019 fiscal year period, was renewed at the end of 2019 for the 2020-2022 fiscal year period. Under that plan, which applies to certain PitchBook employees, awards are tied to financial targets in each year of the plan period, with higher target incentives in the third year of the plan.

value.topic: Integration of the Leveraged Commentary & Data acquisition into PitchBook
value.stated_position: Management said fifty-nine employees joined with the close of the LCD acquisition on June 1, 2022, and that PitchBook has since added staff to support the LCD product across research, product, support, account management, and sales.

investor_qa.quote: Fifty-nine employees joined Morningstar with the close of the LCD acquisition on June 1, 2022. Since then, PitchBook has added staff to support the LCD product including in research, product, support, account management, and sales.

value.topic: Drivers of Morningstar Indexes growth and product partnerships
value.stated_position: Management attributed growth to investable product revenue supported by net inflows to higher margin products and new launches, noting roughly 60 new passive investable products launched with partners including Morgan Stanley, Blackrock, and Citigroup, with particularly strong interest in renewable energy and enhanced ESG indexes.

investor_qa.quote: During the prior year, roughly 60 new passive investable products were launched with partners including Morgan Stanley, Blackrock, and Citigroup. We saw particularly strong interest in products focused on renewable energy and enhanced ESG indexes.

value.topic: Headcount growth plans going into 2023
value.stated_position: "Heading into 2023, we are slowing headcount growth except in our fastest growing product areas. Additionally, we are adding headcount in Wealth Management to support direct indexing and develop our open architecture TAMP, although at a slowing rate." The reduction and shift of China operations is expected to be substantially complete by the end of the third quarter of 2023.

investor_qa.quote: Heading into 2023, we are slowing headcount growth except in our fastest growing product areas. Additionally, we are adding headcount in Wealth Management to support direct indexing and develop our open architecture TAMP, although at a slowing rate.

value.topic: Pricing strategy and pricing power across the portfolio
value.stated_position: "Pricing has been a priority focus for us as we enter 2023 given the inflationary environment." Most success achieving price increases with license-based products; maturity of product does not generally factor into assessments; increases ranging from mid-single-digits to high-single-digits/low-double-digits; harder to raise prices in asset-based areas with "widespread fee compression in the industry."

investor_qa.quote: We are generally implementing higher-than-typical annual price increases for 2023 where appropriate, reflecting the increased value we’re providing as well as increased input costs. Given these factors, we’re instituting price increases ranging from mid-single-digits for certain products to high-single-digits to low-double-digits for other products.

value.topic: Relative importance of corporate versus institutional investor clients for Morningstar Sustainalytics
value.stated_position: "We view the institutional investor and corporate issuer client segments as equally important for the future growth and success of Sustainalytics and believe that they are interdependent." Success with institutional investors drives demand from corporate issuers licensing the ESG rating.

investor_qa.quote: We view the institutional investor and corporate issuer client segments as equally important for the future growth and success of Sustainalytics and believe that they are interdependent.

value.topic: Sustainalytics differentiation through proprietary data
value.stated_position: "Morningstar Sustainalytics offers both proprietary ESG product methodologies and proprietary data sets. The ESG information generally available in the market is unstructured, incomplete, and sometimes of low quality." Data sets cover a 16,000-company universe with current and historical data.

investor_qa.quote: Morningstar Sustainalytics offers both proprietary ESG product methodologies and proprietary data sets. The ESG information generally available in the market is unstructured, incomplete, and sometimes of low quality.

value.topic: DBRS Morningstar competitive position in corporate ratings by geography
value.stated_position: In Canada, "we have a leading market position with a strong presence in corporate ratings with little client turnover"; in the U.S. primarily active in private/middle market; the public investment-grade sector "is dominated by Moody's and S&P" and "it remains difficult for DBRS Morningstar to compete"; in Europe the markets are more open with a growing position.

investor_qa.quote: By contrast, the public investment-grade sector in the U.S. is dominated by Moody’s and S&P, and, given that most non-insurance institutional mandates reference ratings provided by Moody’s, S&P, and Fitch, and use benchmarks that rely on these ratings, it remains difficult for DBRS Morningstar to compete.

value.topic: PitchBook's importance to future growth and product bundling
value.stated_position: "We view PitchBook as important to Morningstar's future growth given the continued convergence of private and public markets, and the increased importance of private debt, which was a driver of our acquisition of LCD." Starting to bundle Morningstar public equity data and ESG ratings into PitchBook, plus the Morningstar Unicorn Index built on PitchBook and Morningstar Indexes capabilities.

investor_qa.quote: We view PitchBook as important to Morningstar’s future growth given the continued convergence of private and public markets, and the increased importance of private debt, which was a driver of our acquisition of LCD. As a result, we have made significant ongoing investments to support its growth.

value.topic: PitchBook total addressable market
value.stated_position: TAM built from number of qualifying firms and estimated average account revenue rather than total licenses; "You can see from the large TAM ($4.9 billion) and our market share estimate that we have a lot of room for growth."

investor_qa.quote: You can see from the large TAM ($4.9 billion) and our market share estimate that we have a lot of room for growth.

value.topic: Cash management and capital allocation approach
value.stated_position: "We continue to balance capital allocation priorities, and our approach has not changed. Historically, we have taken a conservative approach to managing cash and favor short-duration, high-quality, liquid investments." In the current rate environment, also "remain focused on repayment of debt to minimize interest expense."

investor_qa.quote: We continue to balance capital allocation priorities, and our approach has not changed. Historically, we have taken a conservative approach to managing cash and favor short-duration, high-quality, liquid investments.

value.topic: Dividend policy and payout ratio
value.stated_position: "Dividends have consistently been an important part of our capital allocation policy and we are proud to have raised the dividend every year since its inception." No specific payout target; average adjusted payout ratio since 2018 is in the mid-20s; announced a 4.2% quarterly dividend increase and a new $500 million share repurchase program replacing the January 2021 program.

investor_qa.quote: Dividends have consistently been an important part of our capital allocation policy and we are proud to have raised the dividend every year since its inception. We review our dividend policy and capital allocation regularly with our board. We just announced a 4.2% increase in our quarterly dividend payable in 2023 and a new $500 million share repurchase program (replacing the existing program from January 2021).

value.topic: Bonus plan design
value.stated_position: Bonus pool funding based on performance relative to financial targets tied to the annual budget, using adjusted revenue and adjusted EBITDA, "with a floor at 60% funding and no cap."

investor_qa.quote: The bonus plan calculation is based on two performance measures: adjusted revenue and adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization). If adjusted revenue and adjusted EBITDA are realized at 100% of target, the bonus is funded at 100%. The pool increases or decreases based on performance against these goals, with a floor at 60% funding and no cap.

value.topic: Founder Joe Mansueto family holdings
value.stated_position: "All of Joe's holdings are disclosed annually in Morningstar's proxy statement and in Schedule 13G filed with the SEC."

segments_basis.basis: product or business areas described in Item 1 — this filing does not disclose reportable segments, so these are NOT segments and must not be compared with a year that does

investor_qa_basis.basis: management's written answers to questions submitted by investors, published roughly monthly. Same verification as every other fact — whole-document boundaries and a checked quote — but a different kind of evidence from a 10-K or proxy statement: unaudited, unprompted by any disclosure requirement, and responsive to whatever was asked. Corroborating; not a substitute for a filed disclosure.

ids.basis: content hash of the claim, its evidence and its source — see `fact_id` in src/equity_research/ledger_schema.py. Confidence and the verification result are NOT hashed, so re-verifying a fact does not renumber it. Cross-year uniqueness is enforced fatally at build time by `audit_ids`.

document_window.basis: filing dates of the documents this year's facts are actually drawn from — NOT the fiscal window in inventory.json, which bounds the fiscal years in scope. Documents reporting on a fiscal year are filed after it ends, so this range extends past window_end_date by construction. Any accession listed above additionally belongs to a fiscal year outside the window and is used deliberately: an annual-meeting vote held in May of year N decides on year N-1.

applied.evidence: informed Morningstar's Chief Executive Officer that she has decided to depart Morningstar in August 2022
applied.reason: The filing reports an announcement, not a departure. On 2022-05-06 Ms. Desmond informed the CEO of a decision to depart "in August 2022"; her last day was 2023-01-31, recorded separately from the 8-K/A filed 2023-02-02. Recording this as change=departed dated 2022-05-06 put a departure on the timeline on a date it did not happen, and made the two facts look like one event dated two ways.
